subject.title: feat(openrouter): forward OpenClaw session id as session_id

question: Should OpenRouter `forwardSessionId` ship as a provider-owned opt-in that forwards the raw OpenClaw session id, or should it use a derived/provider-scoped key or a different config surface?
rationale: The code path is narrow, but the decision changes public config and sends stable session identity to a third-party provider, which automation should not approve by policy.

options.title: Approve current opt-in
options.body: Accept `plugins.entries.openrouter.config.forwardSessionId` and raw `options.sessionId` egress as the OpenRouter-owned default-off contract.

options.title: Require derived key
options.body: Keep the feature but send a provider-scoped derived affinity key instead of the raw OpenClaw session id.

options.title: Move the config surface
options.body: Revise the option into provider/model params or a broader session-context mechanism before exposing a new plugin config key.

recommendation.title: Approve current opt-in
recommendation.body: Accept `plugins.entries.openrouter.config.forwardSessionId` and raw `options.sessionId` egress as the OpenRouter-owned default-off contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent OpenRouter stream/provider history and repeated adjacent runtime ownership make this the best available routing candidate for the policy call.
